chips.t: You do scanning while reading a schedule about the screen timings of a movie or a cricket match or while going through the weather map in the newspaper.

chips.t: To make the scanning process more helpful, you can use the following strategies:

chips.t: Find out the keyword from the question itself

chips.t: You should scan separately for each question

chips.t: When you re-locate the keyword, go through the surrounding texts too.

chips.t: This is a technique almost similar to that of scanning, but the aim is to collect the main points of the text from a wider perspective. It’s just like skimming milk, where after skimming, we skim the finest part of the milk. Likewise, when you skim a text, you will learn the main points in the text, thereby; you can save your time.
chips.zh: 这是一种几乎类似于扫描的技术，但目的是从更广泛的角度收集文本的要点。就像脱脂牛奶一样，脱脂后，我们把牛奶中最好的部分脱脂。同样，当您浏览文本时，您将了解文本中的要点，从而；你可以节省你的时间。

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter

chips.t: Know What You're Reading – and Why
chips.zh: 知道你在读什么——以及为什么

chips.t: Before you begin, ask yourself three questions:
chips.zh: 在开始之前，问自己三个问题：

chips.t: 1.What is the purpose of the text? For example, is it to entertain, inform, explain, or persuade?
chips.zh: 1.本文的目的是什么？例如，是为了娱乐、告知、解释还是说服？

chips.t: 2.How useful is it? Is it relevant, accurate, impartial, current – or not worth reading?
chips.zh: 2.它有多大用处？它是相关的、准确的、公正的、最新的——还是不值得一读？

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: Follow these steps to read effectively:
chips.zh: 请按照以下步骤进行有效阅读：

chips.t: Use the cover, title page, introduction, and any other general information, to get an overall sense of the content and approach.
chips.zh: 使用封面、扉页、简介和任何其他一般信息，以获得对内容和方法的整体了解。

chips.t: Dip into the text here and there, to tune in to the author's tone of voice.
chips.zh: 深入阅读文本，了解作者的语气。

chips.t: Notice any additional features that might help you to engage with the information.
chips.zh: 请注意任何可能帮助您理解信息的附加功能。

chips.t: Read the Contents, look at how the information is organized, and start spotting the sections that will likely be most important for you.
chips.zh: 阅读目录，查看信息的组织方式，并开始找出对您来说可能最重要的部分。

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: Use chapter headings, abstracts and summaries. Look for illustrations and graphics.
chips.zh: 使用章节标题、摘要和摘要。寻找插图和图形。

chips.t: It helps to know where to look for the key information. So spotting particular structures in writing can help your reading be even more efficient.
chips.zh: 它有助于了解在哪里寻找关键信息。因此，发现写作中的特定结构可以帮助你提高阅读效率。

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: When you need more than just a basic understanding, keep using introductions and summaries, but explore them in more detail.
chips.zh: 当您需要的不仅仅是基本理解时，请继续使用介绍和摘要，但要更详细地探索它们。

chips.t: You can still "speed read" chapters, but spend enough time on the key words and concepts and make sure that you haven't overlooked any important points.
chips.zh: 您仍然可以“快速阅读”章节，但要在关键词和概念上花费足够的时间，并确保您没有忽略任何重要的要点。

chips.t: Pay attention to diagrams, charts and graphs, as they are often used to explain complex ideas within the text.
chips.zh: 注意图表、图表和图表，因为它们通常用于解释文本中的复杂想法。

chips.t: And make simple annotations, or highlight important words and phrases, to ensure that you're reading to the level of detail required.
chips.zh: 并进行简单的注释，或突出显示重要的单词和短语，以确保您阅读到所需的详细程度。

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: When "deep reading" is required, maybe to teach, or to remember for an exam.It’s step-by-step approach involves surveying the material, using key questions to guide you, then thoroughly reading, recalling and reviewing the text. It checks that you really understand what you're reading, and increases your chances of remembering it.
chips.zh: 当需要“深度阅读”时，也许是为了教学，或者为了考试而记忆。它的循序渐进的方法包括调查材料，使用关键问题来指导你，然后彻底阅读、回忆和复习文本。它会检查您是否真正理解正在阅读的内容，并增加您记住它的机会。

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: To give yourself the best chance of reading effectively, always think about where and when to do it.
chips.zh: 为了给自己提供有效阅读的最佳机会，请始终考虑在何时何地进行阅读。

chips.t: For example, in bed, shortly before going to sleep, reading for pleasure might be a good way to relax your mind. But it's likely not the best time or place for in-depth study!
chips.zh: 例如，在床上，临睡前不久，阅读乐趣可能是放松心情的好方法。但这可能不是深入研究的最佳时间或地点！

chips.t: Imagine you've just turned on your TV. You see a man in a suit standing in front of a large map with the symbols of a sun, clouds and thunder. What do you imagine he is about to tell you? Most likely, this is going to be a weather forecast. You can expect to hear words like 'sunny', 'windy' and 'overcast'. You'll probably hear the use of the future tense: 'It'll be a cold start to the day'; 'there'll be showers in the afternoon', etc.
chips.zh: 想象一下您刚刚打开电视。你看到一个穿着西装的男人站在一张大地图前，地图上有太阳、云彩和雷霆的符号。你认为他会告诉你什么？这很可能是天气预报。您可能会听到“晴天”、“有风”和“阴天”等词语。您可能会听到使用将来时：“这将是这一天的冷开始”； “下午有阵雨”等等。

chips.t: If you are taking a listening test, skim through the questions first and try to predict what kind of information you need to listen out for. A question beginning 'How many..?', for example, will probably require you to listen for a specific number or quantity of something.
chips.zh: 如果您正在参加听力测试，请先浏览一下问题并尝试预测您需要聆听哪些类型的信息。例如，以“多少……？”开头的问题可能会要求您聆听某物的特定数字或数量。

chips.t: I magine you are a superhero flying in the sky. From that height, it is possible to see what the entire area is like, how densely populated it is, the kind of houses in each area.
chips.zh: 我想象你是一个在天上飞的超级英雄。从那个高度，可以看到整个区域是什么样子，人口有多么密集，每个区域的房子是什么样的。

chips.t: When listening, it is also possible to get the ‘whole picture’ but with one crucial difference: information comes in a sequence. And in that sequence of information, there are content words (the nouns, adjectives and verbs) that can help you form that picture. We often call this listening for gist.
chips.zh: 聆听时，也可以了解“全貌”，但有一个关键的区别：信息按顺序出现。在该信息序列中，有一些实词（名词、形容词和动词）可以帮助您形成该图片。我们通常称之为“倾听要点”。

chips.t: When you learn new words, try to group them with other words used in a similar context. Mind maps are good for this.
chips.zh: 当您学习新单词时，尝试将它们与类似上下文中使用的其他单词分组。思维导图对此很有用。

chips.t: Just like the traffic lights on roads, there are signposts in language that help us follow what we're listening to. These words, which link ideas, help us to understand what the speaker is talking about and where they are taking us. They're particularly important in presentations and lectures.
chips.zh: 就像道路上的红绿灯一样，语言中的路标可以帮助我们遵循我们所听到的内容。这些词语将思想联系起来，帮助我们理解演讲者在说什么以及他们要把我们带到哪里。它们在演示和讲座中尤其重要。

chips.t: Tip: In your notebook, group signpost phrases according to their functions, and continue to add new expressions as you come across them.
chips.zh: 提示：在笔记本中，根据路标短语的功能对其进行分组，并在遇到它们时继续添加新的表达方式。

chips.t: When listening for details, you are interested in a specific kind of information – perhaps a number, name or object. You can ignore anything that does not sound relevant. In this way, you are able to narrow down your search and get the detail you need.
chips.zh: 当聆听细节时，您对特定类型的信息感兴趣 - 也许是数字、名称或物体。您可以忽略任何听起来不相关的内容。通过这种方式，您可以缩小搜索范围并获得所需的详细信息。

chips.t: In a listening test, if you are asked to write down the age of a person, listen for the words related to age ('old', 'young', 'years', 'date of birth', etc.) or a number that could represent that person's age. If it is a conversation, you might wait to hear someone beginning a question with 'How old…?'
chips.zh: 在听力测试中，如果要求您写下一个人的年龄，请听听与年龄相关的单词（“老”、“年轻”、“岁数”、“出生日期”等）或可以代表该人年龄的数字。如果是对话，您可能会等待听到有人以“多大……？”开始问题。

chips.t: Tip:If you are taking a test, as soon as you get the question paper, skim through the questions, underline the important words and decide what kind of detail you need to identify in the listening text.
chips.zh: 提示：如果您正在参加考试，拿到试卷后，请立即浏览问题，在重要单词下划线，并确定需要在听力文本中识别哪些细节。

chips.t: It is the technique of inferring meaning: using clues and prior knowledge about a situation to work out the meaning of what we hear..
chips.zh: 这是推断意义的技术：利用有关情况的线索和先验知识来推断出我们所听到的含义。

chips.t: Tip: The next time you hear a word you don't understand, try to guess its meaning using the context or situation to help you. But don't worry if you don't get it the first time. As with everything in life, the more you practise , the better you will get.
chips.zh: 提示：下次当您听到不理解的单词时，请尝试使用上下文或情况来猜测其含义以帮助您。但如果您第一次没有得到它，请不要担心。就像生活中的一切一样，你练习得越多，你就会越好。

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: Know What You're Reading – and Why
chips.zh: 知道你在读什么——以及为什么

chips.t: Before you begin, ask yourself three questions:
chips.zh: 在开始之前，问自己三个问题：

chips.t: 1.What is the purpose of the text? For example, is it to entertain, inform, explain, or persuade?
chips.zh: 1.本文的目的是什么？例如，是为了娱乐、告知、解释还是说服？

chips.t: 2.How useful is it? Is it relevant, accurate, impartial, current – or not worth reading?
chips.zh: 2.它有多大用处？它是相关的、准确的、公正的、最新的——还是不值得一读？

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: Follow these steps to read effectively:
chips.zh: 请按照以下步骤进行有效阅读：

chips.t: Use the cover, title page, introduction, and any other general information, to get an overall sense of the content and approach.
chips.zh: 使用封面、扉页、简介和任何其他一般信息，以获得对内容和方法的整体了解。

chips.t: Dip into the text here and there, to tune in to the author's tone of voice.
chips.zh: 深入阅读文本，了解作者的语气。

chips.t: Notice any additional features that might help you to engage with the information.
chips.zh: 请注意任何可能帮助您理解信息的附加功能。

chips.t: Read the Contents, look at how the information is organized, and start spotting the sections that will likely be most important for you.
chips.zh: 阅读目录，查看信息的组织方式，并开始找出对您来说可能最重要的部分。

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: Use chapter headings, abstracts and summaries. Look for illustrations and graphics.
chips.zh: 使用章节标题、摘要和摘要。寻找插图和图形。

chips.t: It helps to know where to look for the key information. So spotting particular structures in writing can help your reading be even more efficient.
chips.zh: 它有助于了解在哪里寻找关键信息。因此，发现写作中的特定结构可以帮助你提高阅读效率。

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: When you need more than just a basic understanding, keep using introductions and summaries, but explore them in more detail.
chips.zh: 当您需要的不仅仅是基本理解时，请继续使用介绍和摘要，但要更详细地探索它们。

chips.t: You can still "speed read" chapters, but spend enough time on the key words and concepts and make sure that you haven't overlooked any important points.
chips.zh: 您仍然可以“快速阅读”章节，但要在关键词和概念上花费足够的时间，并确保您没有忽略任何重要的要点。

chips.t: Pay attention to diagrams, charts and graphs, as they are often used to explain complex ideas within the text.
chips.zh: 注意图表、图表和图表，因为它们通常用于解释文本中的复杂想法。

chips.t: And make simple annotations, or highlight important words and phrases, to ensure that you're reading to the level of detail required.
chips.zh: 并进行简单的注释，或突出显示重要的单词和短语，以确保您阅读到所需的详细程度。

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: When "deep reading" is required, maybe to teach, or to remember for an exam.It’s step-by-step approach involves surveying the material, using key questions to guide you, then thoroughly reading, recalling and reviewing the text. It checks that you really understand what you're reading, and increases your chances of remembering it.
chips.zh: 当需要“深度阅读”时，也许是为了教学，或者为了考试而记忆。它的循序渐进的方法包括调查材料，使用关键问题来指导你，然后彻底阅读、回忆和复习文本。它会检查您是否真正理解正在阅读的内容，并增加您记住它的机会。

chips.t: 5 Ways to Read Faster and Read Smarter
chips.zh: 更快、更聪明阅读的 5 种方法

chips.t: To give yourself the best chance of reading effectively, always think about where and when to do it.
chips.zh: 为了给自己提供有效阅读的最佳机会，请始终考虑在何时何地进行阅读。

chips.t: For example, in bed, shortly before going to sleep, reading for pleasure might be a good way to relax your mind. But it's likely not the best time or place for in-depth study!
chips.zh: 例如，在床上，临睡前不久，阅读乐趣可能是放松心情的好方法。但这可能不是深入研究的最佳时间或地点！

chips.t: Imagine you've just turned on your TV. You see a man in a suit standing in front of a large map with the symbols of a sun, clouds and thunder. What do you imagine he is about to tell you? Most likely, this is going to be a weather forecast. You can expect to hear words like 'sunny', 'windy' and 'overcast'. You'll probably hear the use of the future tense: 'It'll be a cold start to the day'; 'there'll be showers in the afternoon', etc.
chips.zh: 想象一下您刚刚打开电视。你看到一个穿着西装的男人站在一张大地图前，地图上有太阳、云彩和雷霆的符号。你认为他会告诉你什么？这很可能是天气预报。您可能会听到“晴天”、“有风”和“阴天”等词语。您可能会听到使用将来时：“这将是这一天的冷开始”； “下午有阵雨”等等。

chips.t: If you are taking a listening test, skim through the questions first and try to predict what kind of information you need to listen out for. A question beginning 'How many..?', for example, will probably require you to listen for a specific number or quantity of something.
chips.zh: 如果您正在参加听力测试，请先浏览一下问题并尝试预测您需要聆听哪些类型的信息。例如，以“多少……？”开头的问题可能会要求您聆听某物的特定数字或数量。

chips.t: I magine you are a superhero flying in the sky. From that height, it is possible to see what the entire area is like, how densely populated it is, the kind of houses in each area.
chips.zh: 我想象你是一个在天上飞的超级英雄。从那个高度，可以看到整个区域是什么样子，人口有多么密集，每个区域的房子是什么样的。

chips.t: When listening, it is also possible to get the ‘whole picture’ but with one crucial difference: information comes in a sequence. And in that sequence of information, there are content words (the nouns, adjectives and verbs) that can help you form that picture. We often call this listening for gist.
chips.zh: 聆听时，也可以了解“全貌”，但有一个关键的区别：信息按顺序出现。在该信息序列中，有一些实词（名词、形容词和动词）可以帮助您形成该图片。我们通常称之为“倾听要点”。

chips.t: When you learn new words, try to group them with other words used in a similar context. Mind maps are good for this.
chips.zh: 当您学习新单词时，尝试将它们与类似上下文中使用的其他单词分组。思维导图对此很有用。

chips.t: Just like the traffic lights on roads, there are signposts in language that help us follow what we're listening to. These words, which link ideas, help us to understand what the speaker is talking about and where they are taking us. They're particularly important in presentations and lectures.
chips.zh: 就像道路上的红绿灯一样，语言中的路标可以帮助我们遵循我们所听到的内容。这些词语将思想联系起来，帮助我们理解演讲者在说什么以及他们要把我们带到哪里。它们在演示和讲座中尤其重要。

chips.t: Tip: In your notebook, group signpost phrases according to their functions, and continue to add new expressions as you come across them.
chips.zh: 提示：在笔记本中，根据路标短语的功能对其进行分组，并在遇到它们时继续添加新的表达方式。

chips.t: When listening for details, you are interested in a specific kind of information – perhaps a number, name or object. You can ignore anything that does not sound relevant. In this way, you are able to narrow down your search and get the detail you need.
chips.zh: 当聆听细节时，您对特定类型的信息感兴趣 - 也许是数字、名称或物体。您可以忽略任何听起来不相关的内容。通过这种方式，您可以缩小搜索范围并获得所需的详细信息。

chips.t: In a listening test, if you are asked to write down the age of a person, listen for the words related to age ('old', 'young', 'years', 'date of birth', etc.) or a number that could represent that person's age. If it is a conversation, you might wait to hear someone beginning a question with 'How old…?'
chips.zh: 在听力测试中，如果要求您写下一个人的年龄，请听听与年龄相关的单词（“老”、“年轻”、“岁数”、“出生日期”等）或可以代表该人年龄的数字。如果是对话，您可能会等待听到有人以“多大……？”开始问题。

chips.t: Tip:If you are taking a test, as soon as you get the question paper, skim through the questions, underline the important words and decide what kind of detail you need to identify in the listening text.
chips.zh: 提示：如果您正在参加考试，拿到试卷后，请立即浏览问题，在重要单词下划线，并确定需要在听力文本中识别哪些细节。

chips.t: It is the technique of inferring meaning: using clues and prior knowledge about a situation to work out the meaning of what we hear..
chips.zh: 这是推断意义的技术：利用有关情况的线索和先验知识来推断出我们所听到的含义。

chips.t: Tip: The next time you hear a word you don't understand, try to guess its meaning using the context or situation to help you. But don't worry if you don't get it the first time. As with everything in life, the more you practise , the better you will get.
chips.zh: 提示：下次当您听到不理解的单词时，请尝试使用上下文或情况来猜测其含义以帮助您。但如果您第一次没有得到它，请不要担心。就像生活中的一切一样，你练习得越多，你就会越好。

chips.t: The fall of a Mayan city

Many years before, when the king was looking for somewhere to live, he saw a big beautiful ceiba tree in the heart of the tropical rainforest. He decided that it was the perfect place to make his home. Just as he was about to leave an old man appeared from behind the tree.
chips.zh: 许多年前，当国王寻找住处时，他在热带雨林的中心看到了一棵美丽的木棉树。他认为这是安家的最佳地点。正当他要离开的时候，树后出现了一位老人。

chips.t: We have always looked after the rainforest and you must too/ he said. 'Don't chop down the trees! Build your city somewhere else!' And he disappeared into the forest again.
chips.zh: 我们一直在照顾雨林，你也必须这样做/他说。 “不要砍伐树木！在别处建造你的城市！然后他又消失在森林里了。

chips.t: But the king ignored the old man's advice’ He's just a crazy old man, he thought to himself. And he built his city nearby. As the king and his people became richer and more powerful the city grew and grew. People needed more space to build their houses and grow their corn. So they chopped down more and more trees from the rainforest.
chips.zh: 但国王没有理睬老人的建议。他心里想，他只是个疯狂的老人。他在附近建造了自己的城市。随着国王和他的人民变得更加富有和强大，这座城市不断发展壮大。人们需要更多的空间来建造房屋和种植玉米。因此他们从雨林中砍伐了越来越多的树木。

chips.t: Everything seemed perfect, until one day things started to change. At first it didn’t rain as much as it usually did and the rivers became smaller and smaller. Then it stopped raining and the rivers dried up. The corn in the fields and the vegetables in the gardens dried up, too. With little food and water, the people started to leave the city The king was very worried. 'What can I do?’ he asked his advisors.
chips.zh: 一切看起来都很完美，直到有一天事情开始发生变化。起初，雨没有平时那么多，河水也变得越来越小。后来雨停了，河水也干了。地里的玉米和花园里的蔬菜也都干了。由于食物和水所剩无几，人们开始离开城市。国王非常担心。 “我能做什么？”他问他的顾问。

chips.t: None of them could give him an answer. Then he remembered the old man he met in the forest. He went back and looked for the tall ceiba tree. Eventually he found it but now it was standing alone in the middle of a desert. He sat under its branches in the shade.
chips.zh: 他们都无法给他答案。然后他想起了他在森林里遇到的那个老人。他回去寻找那棵高大的木棉树。最终他找到了它，但现在它孤零零地矗立在沙漠中央。他坐在树荫下的树枝下。

chips.t: Suddenly, the same old man came out from behind the tree.
chips.zh: 突然，同样的老人从树后走了出来。

chips.t: Who came out from behind the tree?
'Look what you've done,' said the old man.
The king fell to his knees and asked, 'Please tell me – what should I do?'
chips.zh: 国王跪下问道：“请告诉我——我该怎么办？”

chips.t: What is the old man’s suggestion?
'Well there is a solution but it will take many, many years, the old man said. This time, the king listened carefully to every word.
chips.zh: “嗯，有一个解决方案，但需要很多很多年，”老人说。这一次，国王认真地听着每一个字。

chips.t: 'If you plant two trees for every one you chopped down then maybe the rain will return and maybe the rivers, the plants, the birds and the animals will come back,' the old man said, and suddenly disappeared, just like before.
chips.zh: “如果你每砍倒一棵树，就种两棵树，也许雨水会回来，也许河流、植物、鸟类和动物会回来。”老人说着，突然消失了，就像以前一样。

chips.t: Quickly, the king ordered his people to plant trees where there was now desert. Slowly but surely, as the years passed, the trees grew, the rain came back and the rainforest filled with life again.
chips.zh: 国王很快命令他的人民在现在沙漠的地方植树。慢慢地，但可以肯定的是，随着岁月的流逝，树木长大了，雨水又回来了，雨林再次充满了生机。

chips.t: First the animals and birds returned and then the people. The king was delighted.
chips.zh: 首先是动物和鸟类回归，然后是人类。国王很高兴。

chips.t: Before he died he made sure that the ceiba tree was always protected, so that his people would look after the rainforest.
chips.zh: 在他去世之前，他确保木棉树始终受到保护，以便他的人民能够照顾雨林。

The Mayan king looked down at the city from his palace. He felt very sad. He could remember the brightly coloured pyramids and temples; the exotic gardens full of jaguars, pumas and parrots and the buzzing street markets with delicious food from all over his empire. It was one of the great wonders of the world. But now the city was silent and empty. And why was this ...?
chips.zh: 玛雅国王从他的宫殿俯瞰这座城市。他感到非常难过。他还记得色彩鲜艳的金字塔和寺庙；充满美洲虎、美洲狮和鹦鹉的异国情调花园，以及出售来自他的帝国各地的美味食物的热闹街头市场。这是世界最伟大的奇迹之一。但现在这座城市一片寂静，空荡荡的。为什么这是……？

chips.t: The fall of a Mayan city

Many years before, when the king was looking for somewhere to live, he saw a big beautiful ceiba tree in the heart of the tropical rainforest. He decided that it was the perfect place to make his home. Just as he was about to leave ,an old man appeared from behind the tree.
chips.zh: 许多年前，当国王寻找住处时，他在热带雨林的中心看到了一棵美丽的木棉树。他认为这是安家的最佳地点。正当他要离开的时候，树后出现了一个老者。

chips.t: We have always looked after the rainforest and you must, too. he said. 'Don't chop down the trees! Build your city somewhere else!' And he disappeared into the forest again.
chips.zh: 我们一直在保护雨林，您也必须如此。他说。 “不要砍伐树木！在别处建造你的城市！然后他又消失在森林里了。

chips.t: But the king ignored the old man's advice’ He's just a crazy old man, he thought to himself. And he built his city nearby. As the king and his people became richer and more powerful the city grew and grew. People needed more space to build their houses and grow their corn. So they chopped down more and more trees from the rainforest.
chips.zh: 但国王没有理睬老人的建议。他心里想，他只是个疯狂的老人。他在附近建造了自己的城市。随着国王和他的人民变得更加富有和强大，这座城市不断发展壮大。人们需要更多的空间来建造房屋和种植玉米。因此他们从雨林中砍伐了越来越多的树木。

chips.t: Everything seemed perfect, until one day things started to change. At first it didn’t rain as much as it usually did and the rivers became smaller and smaller. Then it stopped raining and the rivers dried up. The corn in the fields and the vegetables in the gardens dried up, too. With little food and water, the people started to leave the city The king was very worried. 'What can I do?’ he asked his advisors.
chips.zh: 一切看起来都很完美，直到有一天事情开始发生变化。起初，雨没有平时那么多，河水也变得越来越小。后来雨停了，河水也干了。地里的玉米和花园里的蔬菜也都干了。由于食物和水所剩无几，人们开始离开城市。国王非常担心。 “我能做什么？”他问他的顾问。

chips.t: None of them could give him an answer. Then he remembered the old man he met in the forest. He went back and looked for the tall ceiba tree. Eventually he found it but now it was standing alone in the middle of a desert. He sat under its branches in the shade.
chips.zh: 他们都无法给他答案。然后他想起了他在森林里遇到的那个老人。他回去寻找那棵高大的木棉树。最终他找到了它，但现在它孤零零地矗立在沙漠中央。他坐在树荫下的树枝下。

chips.t: Suddenly, the same old man came out from behind the tree.
chips.zh: 突然，同样的老人从树后走了出来。

chips.t: 'Look what you've done,' said the old man.
The king fell to his knees and asked, 'Please tell me – what should I do?'
chips.zh: 国王跪下问道：“请告诉我——我该怎么办？”

chips.t: 'Well there is a solution but it will take many, many years, the old man said. This time, the king listened carefully to every word.
chips.zh: “嗯，有一个解决方案，但需要很多很多年，”老人说。这一次，国王认真地听着每一个字。

chips.t: 'If you plant two trees for every one you chopped down then maybe the rain will return and maybe the rivers, the plants, the birds and the animals will come back,' the old man said, and suddenly disappeared, just like before.
chips.zh: “如果你每砍倒一棵树，就种两棵树，也许雨水会回来，也许河流、植物、鸟类和动物会回来。”老人说着，突然消失了，就像以前一样。

chips.t: Quickly, the king ordered his people to plant trees where there was now desert. Slowly but surely, as the years passed, the trees grew, the rain came back and the rainforest filled with life again.
chips.zh: 国王很快命令他的人民在现在沙漠的地方植树。慢慢地，但可以肯定的是，随着岁月的流逝，树木长大了，雨水又回来了，雨林再次充满了生机。

chips.t: First the animals and birds returned and then the people. The king was delighted.
chips.zh: 首先是动物和鸟类回归，然后是人类。国王很高兴。

chips.t: Before he died he made sure that the ceiba tree was always protected, so that his people would look after the rainforest.
chips.zh: 在他去世之前，他确保木棉树始终受到保护，以便他的人民能够照顾雨林。
